summary: Compact bordered card that groups overview-page actions, optional values or status tags, and native destinations into named sections.
useWhen: An overview rail needs a compact action center with multiple named groups.
Action rows need optional counts or short values aligned at the trailing edge.
Related reports or resource destinations belong beside attention items in one bounded surface.
avoidWhen: The complete card leads to one destination; use CardNavigation.
The surface edits settings in place; use CardSetting.
The content is a chart, legend, metric visualization, or other data-visualization composition; use CardChart or CardOverview.
Rows require descriptions, nested controls, menus, or selection state instead of one direct action.

alternatives.when: The entire surface represents one destination.
alternatives.reason: CardNavigation provides the single native-link card contract.

alternatives.when: The card presents page-level score and metric summaries.
alternatives.reason: CardOverview owns summary metrics, comparison periods, and selectable metric cells.

accessibility: Each non-empty group is a section labelled by an h2 heading, and each row is a native button or link.
Use href for real destinations so link context menus, modified clicks, and native browser semantics remain available.
Prevent the cancelable dsAction event only when an application router takes ownership of the same link activation.
Inactive items become disabled buttons and are removed from keyboard navigation rather than exposing a false destination.
Keep item labels concise; a visible trailing value participates in the action's accessible name.
states: Rows expose distinct rest, hover, pressed, keyboard-focus, and inactive states.
An empty sections array or groups with no items render the configured empty message.
The application owns loading, error, permission, routing, and post-activation consequences and reflects availability through the supplied item data.
responsiveBehavior: The card fills its parent width and never establishes a product breakpoint.
Long labels wrap while trailing values remain visible; the page owns rail width and movement below primary content.
Groups retain their order when the parent layout moves the complete card between desktop and mobile regions.

customElements: Assign sections as a JavaScript property; complex arrays are not supported as string attributes.
Listen for dsAction and inspect sectionId, itemId, item, and the original pointer event.
react: Pass sections as an array and handle onDsAction for product actions or client-side routing.
Prevent the event only when replacing native navigation for an item with href.
angular: Bind [sections] through the generated standalone adapter and inspect $event.detail from (dsAction).
Keep product data and activation consequences in the Angular owner rather than embedding them in the component contract.
